definition: The feast of Saint Michael and All Angels, observed on September 29; traditionally one of England’s quarter days, when rents were due and terms began or ended.
etymology: Middle English joined Michael, the archangel’s name, to Mass: literally, “Michael’s Mass.” The name became attached not only to the feast but to the legal and agricultural turn of the season around it.
usage: With Michaelmas near, the tenancy was renewed and the hedgerows had begun to redden with haws.
